note: Conformance vectors for a roadmap's line grammar: what a project's
project/ROADMAP.md says it claims, and what each claim names as showing it.
Shared, not owned: qmcp tour reads roadmaps, and so does
project-seed/ci/check_roadmap.py, and neither imports the other.
`lines` is what a reader reads the roadmap as, in its order: the group it
stands under, the claim with its names taken out, whether it is ticked, and
the journeys and walkthrough pages it names. The expected readings are
Adding a case is cheap, and is the right response to a roadmap read
wrongly in the wild. Removing one needs a reason.

cases.name: a group and a ticked line naming a journey
cases.why: the ordinary line: the heading is its group, and the journey's name leaves the claim
cases.roadmap:
## Making a thing

- [x] A part is chosen, shaped and printed. `journey:make`

lines.text: A part is chosen, shaped and printed.

cases.name: an unticked line naming a page by a relative link with a fragment
cases.why: a page is known by its file name, whatever prefix and fragment its link carries

cases.name: a line naming a journey and two pages
cases.why: each name leaves the claim with the commas and spaces that follow it
cases.roadmap:
## Starting

- [x] A fresh clone is served. `journey:start`, [00](../../../walkthrough/00-getting-started.md), [10](../../../walkthrough/10-serving-it.md)

cases.name: a line continued on indented lines
cases.why: indented lines under an item continue it, and a name on them belongs to the line

lines.text: A long claim that goes on here, and names at the end.

cases.name: a nested list item is not part of the line
cases.why: a bullet under an item is its own thing, so a name in it does not show the line

lines.text: A claim with a note below it.

cases.name: a fenced block holds no lines
cases.why: a roadmap can show its own format without claiming anything

cases.name: a heading of another level opens no group
cases.why: only a `## ` heading opens a group; a `### ` heading leaves the line in the group above it

cases.name: a journey written outside a code span is prose
cases.why: the grammar names a journey only in a code span, so this line is shown by nothing

lines.text: Shown by journey:make in plain words.

cases.name: a page named in a code span without a link is prose
cases.why: the grammar names a page only by a link, so this line is shown by nothing

cases.name: a line above the first group
cases.why: a line before any `## ` heading has no group

cases.name: other bullets and a capital X
cases.why: `*` and `+` bullets are items too, and `[X]` is ticked
cases.roadmap:
## G

* [X] A starred line. `journey:a`
+ [ ] A plus line. `journey:b`

cases.name: a name given twice is one name
cases.why: a journey or page named twice on a line is listed once

cases.name: a journey id with a capital is prose
cases.why: a journey id is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, so `journey:Make` names nothing
